summary: P0 bug fix verified end-to-end: order_counter NEVER decrements during the day. 9/9 backend pytest cases pass. Covered: single delete keeps counter, 3 consecutive deletes keep MAX, new order after delete uses counter+1 (no reuse), delete-all keeps counter and continues from MAX+1, archived-today is included in MAX, midnight_reset atomic (orders empty / archived has all / counter=0), recover_stale_orders archives yesterday but spares today, plus POST/GET /api/orders regression.
critical_code_review_comments: delete_order (server.py L737-783) correctly delegates counter recompute to _highest_order_number_today() which takes MAX over (active orders, archived_orders today, deletion_logs today). This is the right fix - the bug pre-fix used only active orders.

midnight_reset uses _atomic_archive_and_clear: insert_many is verified by inserted_count BEFORE delete_many runs. If insert_many partially fails, source is preserved. Counter reset to 0 only happens AFTER archive succeeds. Strong correctness.

_highest_order_number_today uses the bounded date window via _today_rome_bounds_utc (Europe/Rome midnight → +24h). created_at and deleted_at are stored as UTC ISO strings; lexical $gte/$lt comparison on ISO 8601 strings is correct because the format is sortable.

recover_stale_orders at startup (server.py L2417) is idempotent and safe: only archives orders where created_at < today's Rome midnight, then recomputes per-restaurant order_counter from remaining-today data. Won't touch fresh orders. Handles boot after downtime cleanly.

POTENTIAL EDGE CASE (not blocking): create_order's $inc-then-read can race under concurrent POSTs from the same restaurant on motor (find_one_and_update with $inc IS atomic on the document so this is fine - just noting). However the `if data.order_number` branch uses a conditional update that is NOT atomic with the subsequent insert: if two clients pass the same higher number, both inserts will succeed with the SAME order_number. Recommend either dropping the client-provided order_number path or adding a unique index on (restaurant_id, order_number) with retry. Low risk in current tablet UX (clients don't pass order_number) but worth noting.
SUGGESTION: Replace deprecated @app.on_event("startup")/("shutdown") with FastAPI lifespan (DeprecationWarning visible during tests). Cosmetic only.

deletion_logs documents do NOT include `order_id`; the `id` field is a separate uuid for the log entry. Acceptable, but if you ever want to undo a deletion you'd need to add `original_id`. Non-blocking.
server.py is 2426 lines - splitting into routers (orders.py, magazzino.py, etc.) would help maintainability. Tracked in iteration_4.
seed_data_creation: All TEST_-prefixed orders cleaned up via autouse fixture before AND after each test. Restaurant order_counter, deletion_logs and archived_orders for restaurant 'Flaminio' are scrubbed and reset to 0 between tests, so production data state is restored at end of run (counter back to 0, no test orders left).
context_for_next_testing_agent: P0 counter-decrement bug is FIXED and fully covered by /app/backend/tests/test_order_counter_p0.py. The shared event_loop fixture is required for tests that call server.midnight_reset / recover_stale_orders directly because motor binds to the first asyncio loop it sees. To run: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL + MONGO_URL + DB_NAME env vars must be exported (see existing other test files for pattern). Cleanup is autouse so the suite is rerunnable safely.
rca_of_the_issue: ROOT CAUSE (pre-fix): delete_order set order_counter = highest active-order number after deletion. If all/most orders for the day had already been completed/archived (or the deleted order was the highest active one with lower-numbered active siblings), the counter would jump backwards. The next POST /api/orders would then hand out a number already used today, causing duplicates downstream (Excel export, Bollitore tablet). FIX (verified): _highest_order_number_today() takes MAX across active orders + archived_orders today + deletion_logs today. delete_order writes that MAX to order_counter, so the counter is monotonic during the day. midnight_reset atomically archives + clears + zeroes the counter (so a new day starts at 1). recover_stale_orders self-heals at boot if midnight_reset never ran. REPRO STEPS (also a passing test): create N orders → delete the last K → previously counter would drop to N-K, now stays at N. New order = N+1.
